Now I have the content from the arXiv API. Let me parse the XML to extract the paper details properly.

```python
import re
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

content = result['content']

# Parse the XML
root = ET.fromstring(content)

# Define namespaces
ns = {
    'atom': 'http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom',
    'arxiv': 'http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom'
}

papers = []
for entry in root.findall('atom:entry', ns):
    paper = {}
    paper['title'] = entry.find('atom:title', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    paper['id'] = entry.find('atom:id', ns).text
    paper['summary'] = entry.find('atom:summary', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    paper['published'] = entry.find('atom:published', ns).text
    
    # Get authors
    authors = []
    for author in entry.findall('atom:author', ns):
        name = author.find('atom:name', ns)
        if name is not None:
            authors.append(name.text)
    paper['authors'] = authors
    
    # Get categories/links
    paper['arxiv_id'] = paper['id'].split('/abs/')[-1]
    
    papers.append(paper)

print(f"Found {len(papers)} papers")
for i, p in enumerate(papers):
    print(f"\n--- Paper {i+1} ---")
    print(f"Title: {p['title']}")
    print(f"ID: {p['arxiv_id']}")
    print(f"Published: {p['published']}")
    print(f"Authors: {', '.join(p['authors'][:3])}...")
    print(f"Summary (first 200 chars): {p['summary'][:200]}")
```
